title: MongoDB Repositories
summary: Declare repository methods and understand save and lookup behavior.

richText: A repository provides methods for storing and reading documents.
Spring Data creates the implementation of a MongoRepository interface and registers it as a Spring bean.
The first type argument is the document class. The second is its ID type.
Method names such as findByTitle define derived queries. The property name must exist on the mapped class.

example.title: Declare a journal entry repository
description: Use JournalEntry from the document mapping page.
Place this interface under the application package.
explanation: The repository provides save, findById, findAll and deleteById.
A misspelled property can prevent repository creation.

richText: save inserts a new document or saves a document with an existing ID.
Saving with an existing ID can replace stored fields. Do not use a partially populated request object as a full document replacement.
findById returns Optional because the document may not exist.
findByTitle returns an empty list when nothing matches. A connection failure is a different result.
For a growing collection, use bounded queries or pagination instead of findAll.

example.title: Save and look up an entry
description: Run this code inside a service method with an injected JournalEntryRepository named repository.
explanation: save returns the saved entry, including its generated ID.
findById uses that ID to read the document.
found contains the entry if the document still exists.
